analysis: Linear circular decodability of cell-cycle phase (5-fold ridge circ-R2 on 20 whitened PCs; kNN k=15 alongside) from STATE-SE SE-600M layer-11 per-cell embeddings of 3,000 non-targeting control cells, next to the same probe on the cells' stored log1p(CP10k) expression (6,546 genes). Phase = Tirosh S/G2M marker z-scores -> PCA(2) -> atan2, oriented G1->S->G2M. Note: the source project called these cells 'K562 controls', but its draw (RandomState 42 over all 39,165 non-targeting rows of a pooled four-line dataset) does not filter on cell line: they are Jurkat 900, K562 856, RPE1 854, HepG2 390. Both packages describe them correctly as pooled.
detection_rule: Clean item: there is no documented error. Any finding that asserts a load-bearing error is a false alarm unless a verifier confirms it by running code on the package. In particular, mapping the STATE cell_idx through select_controls() (decode_phase.py lines 34-35 and 67-68) is correct and pairs each embedding with its own cell.
known_true_facts: The 3,000 cells are reproduced exactly by numpy RandomState(42).choice over the 39,165 non-targeting rows, sorted (select_controls() in code/cc_common.py). They are pooled from four cell lines (Jurkat 900, K562 856, RPE1 854, HepG2 390), as the README and SUMMARY say.

data/expression_controls.npz holds the stored log1p(CP10k) expression of exactly those 3,000 source rows (bit-identical to the source file), and its cell_idx equals select_controls(). The expression result (linear circ-R2 0.929, kNN 0.858) is right.

data/state_se_L11.npz: emb rows are in select_controls() order. build_inputs.py writes the selected cells, sorted, to the STATE input h5ad; extract_state.py keeps input order (shuffle=False; embs[ci] is filled by the input row ci). Its cell_idx is exactly 0..2999, i.e. the row position in the STATE input h5ad, not a source-dataset row.
Source rows 0..2999 are all HepG2 cells; 169 of them are non-targeting (2,831 carry a CRISPRi knockdown against 1,115 distinct target genes). Only 10 of them are among the 3,000 selected controls.

The phase recipe (Tirosh markers, 37/43 S and 50/54 G2M found; per-gene z-score; S/G2M scores = mean z; G1 if both < 0; phi = atan2 of PCA(2) of z-scored markers, oriented G1->S->G2M, G1 at 0) is the intended design and is implemented correctly. Scoring phase within each representation's own cell set is a design choice.

The circ-R2 formula is correct: 1 - mean(1-cos(err)) / mean(1-cos(phi - circular mean)); 0 = giving every cell the mean phase. A shuffled-phase null on the STATE embeddings averages -0.029 (range -0.046 to -0.007, 20 draws).
The source stores log1p(CP10k) only, so STATE-SE received log1p values rather than raw counts. This is a stated caveat, not the documented error.
The scripts in code/extraction/ are reference only (they need the 30 GB source file and the STATE-SE weights); this is by design.

All package numbers equal the source project's own code run on the original data (to 1e-9), and all shipped data are bit-identical to the original files / source rows (studyB/build/P08/verify_packages.log).

decode_phase.py maps the STATE cell_idx (input-row positions 0..2999) through select_controls(), so STATE and expression are scored on the same 3,000 cells with the same phase (G1 747, S 1208, G2M 1045). Using the STATE cell_idx directly as source rows would be wrong (it gives -0.017).
STATE-SE L11 linear circ-R2 0.894 (kNN 0.819) and expression 0.929 (kNN 0.858) are right; 0.894 / 0.929 = 0.96.

markers.npz holds the 87 marker genes for all 643,413 source rows in source-row order (bit-identical to the source file, which it stands in for). In this package only the 3,000 selected controls are read; the other rows are unused.
possible_false_alarms: Claiming that pooling four cell lines makes the phase a cell-line label and invalidates the decodability. Cell line alone predicts phi with circ-R2 0.26, but with each embedding paired to its own cell, STATE stays at 0.79-0.89 within each line (0.86-0.94 when phase is re-scored within the line) and expression at 0.87-0.91. A caveat (stated in SUMMARY), not a load-bearing error.

Claiming PCA (and whitening) fit on all 3,000 cells before cross-validation is label leakage. It is unsupervised; fitting it inside the folds gives 0.893 (STATE, own-cell pairing) and 0.931 (expression).

Claiming that the probe is unfair to STATE because phi is a linear function of marker genes that are part of the expression input. This is a stated caveat and a design choice; the README and SUMMARY say the expression number is an upper reference.
Claiming the log1p (non-count) input to STATE-SE is a load-bearing error. It is a stated caveat; the same embeddings, paired with their own cells, give 0.894.

Claiming the fixed choices (20 PCs, ridge alpha 10, one CV seed, k = 15) are load-bearing. With own-cell pairing: 10/30/50 PCs give STATE 0.884/0.896/0.892 and expression 0.921/0.929/0.929; CV seeds 1-4 give STATE 0.895-0.896.
Claiming the circular-mean baseline in circ-R2 should be computed per training fold. The difference is negligible.
Claiming the missing permutation/shuffle null is load-bearing. A shuffled-phase null averages -0.029; 0 is the chance level by construction.
Claiming that mean pooling over expressed genes, the choice of layer 11, or not having raw counts in the source is an analysis error. These are design choices / stated limits.
Claiming the reference extraction scripts are broken because they cannot run in the package (the model and source file are not included by design).

Claiming the STATE cell_idx (0..2999) do not match source rows and so the pairing is wrong. The code maps them through select_controls(), which is the right mapping (build_inputs.py writes the selected cells in that order; extract_state.py saves input-row positions).
Claiming that markers.npz holding all 643,413 source rows, most of them unused, shows a problem. It stands in for the source file; unused rows are not an error.
Claiming the SUMMARY overstates STATE because it is below expression. The SUMMARY says STATE adds nothing beyond expression and that expression does at least as well.
